noscript.heading: Windows and Nevada rules
noscript.intro: Pick a shade for each window below, then call or text us and tell us your picks.

items.title: Build it
items.text: Pick your vehicle, then a shade for each window. Change anything as often as you like.

items.title: Read us the code
items.text: Your build code tells us the vehicle and every shade you picked, so the call is short.

items.title: See it for real
items.text: At the shop, ask to see the film on your glass before we start.

legal_footer: Illustration only. Rules can change; check the current statute. This is not legal advice. NRS 484D.440.

front_ok.long: Nevada requires film plus factory glass to let through at least 35% of light, with a 7% tolerance, and the film must be nonreflective. Factory glass lowers the total, so the shop checks your car. NRS 484D.440.

front_blocked.long: Below Nevada's front-door limit. Not available for road use.

rear.long: Nevada sets no darkness limit here if both outside mirrors show at least 200 feet behind you. NRS 484D.440.

strip.long: Nevada allows windshield tint on the top strip only, above a bottom-edge height the statute sets, and the strip cannot be red or amber. NRS 484D.440.

strip_with_29_inch_figure.long: Nevada allows windshield tint on the top strip only. The bottom edge must be at least 29 inches above the driver's seat, and the strip cannot be red or amber. NRS 484D.440.
strip_with_29_inch_figure.status: PENDING CHASE RULING: overhaul brief section 9 item 9. The 29 inch figure is not yet in the verified list in area-profile.md, so customer copy may not use it until Chase adds it. When he does, copy this long text into strip.long above.
